How Low Are U.S. Taxes Compared to Other Countries?

For "personal tax rates of $100,000 around the world. The U.S. comes in at 55th out of 114." But these numbers might understate how low taxes have been in the U.S. Unlike most advanced economies, the U.S. don't supplement personal income taxes with a national sales tax, or value-added tax (VAT). Consumption taxes accounted for about a fifth of total U.S. revenue in 2008 (mostly at the state and local level) compared to an OECD average of 32 percent. In other words, the U.S. relies uniquely on personal tax rates to raise revenue -- and we have relatively low personal tax rates. The best way to answer the question "Are U.S. taxes high or low compared to other countries?" is to look at taxes as a share of the economy. To answer just in the context of what knowledge you could bring back, here are the easiest things off the top of my head:

If you could find a proficient glassmaker - glass goes back to 3500 BC - you might even be able to build a microscope. And if you can build a microscope, you can build a telescope and now you have kicked off the golden age of astronomy a few thousand years early as well.
